subject: [Pivotal Retail] Intermittent request stalls causing p99 spikes — escalation
messages:
From: Sam Ortega <ops@pivotalretail.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production degradation — checkout paths stalling

Marcus —

We started seeing intermittent stalls across our checkout pipeline this morning (around 07:45 PDT). Symptoms: p99 latencies for Redwood calls jumping to ~28–35s for ~3–7 minute windows, and request error rate climbing from baseline 0.2% to ~4–6% during spikes. Throughput drops as many requests time out and retry. This is customer-facing on the web checkout path — we're seeing ~3% conversion loss during the spikes.

I attached a short log excerpt and a couple of request IDs where the server-level traces show long waits in the inference tier. We're on your Dedicated cluster (cluster-id: pr-retail-ded-02).

Can we get a priority triage? This is impacting live traffic and we'd like an ETA on mitigation.

Thanks,
Sam Ortega
SRE Manager, Pivotal Retail

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sam Ortega <ops@pivotalretail.com>

Sam — thanks for the quick signal and logs. I'm opening a short war-room and adding engineering.

Immediate plan: 
- Kimberly & Dev: can you triage the cluster target (pr-retail-ded-02) for concurrent worker saturation, queue growth, and backpressure propagation?
- Sam: please share any quick Grafana links for the span so we can correlate (token-level latency, queue length, concurrency caps).
- Monica: I want to keep the execs informed if we need to request a burst or credits.

I'll coordinate status and block any external exec pings until we have a hypothesis.

Next update in 30 minutes.

— Marcus
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, Sam Ortega <ops@pivotalretail.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production degradation — checkout paths stalling

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Observed repeated short windows where inferences on pr-retail-ded-02 show a sharp rise in queue length for worker-pool-3. p95 remains fine, but p99 and above diverge.
- Concurrency cap (configured at 64 concurrent requests per replica) is being hit in bursts; autoscaler hasn't added replicas yet due to burst duration being < 5m in current policy.
- KV cache miss churn increases during the windows (likely cold segments + prefix variance), which exacerbates per-token compute and stretches execution time.
- Backpressure ripple: once one replica hits cap, downstream routing pushes to fewer replicas and those hit caps too — a cascading saturation pattern.

Immediate mitigations to try (low-risk):
1) Temporarily raise concurrency cap to 128 on the affected pool.
2) Enable request shedding at 10s to avoid extreme tail blocking other traffic (we'll track error surface).
3) Force-enable short-term prefix-level caching for the checkout model to reduce KV thrash (config flag).

I'll instrument a short telemetry dashboard and add the relevant query links. If the above doesn't reduce p99 within the next 20–30 minutes we'll look at routing partial traffic to our eu-fallback pool while we stabilize.

— Kim
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: Sam Ortega <ops@pivotalretail.com>, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production degradation — checkout paths stalling

Running the mitigations now:
- Concurrency cap bumped to 120 (rounded, want to avoid brittle 128 switch while autoscaler rules are being evaluated).
- Shedding=10s enabled and monitored (we'll count earlier-level retries).
- Pinned a quantized lower-capacity model variant for the hot checkout route as a fallback (model-id: rwd-checkout-q4) — this is a temporary performance-first fallback, quality delta small for system prompts used in checkout.
- Enabled prefix caching flag for the route and warmed a few hot prefixes.

Early notes after 14 minutes: p99 has dropped from 32s -> ~12–15s during the late part of the previous window. Error rate reduced from ~5% -> ~1.2%. Throughput recovered by ~65% vs peak-impacted minute. We'll keep telemetry streaming into the war-room.

Attachments: mitigation_playbook.pdf (playbook excerpt: steps we executed, rollback procedures).

Next: I recommend we open a short ticket (SUP-4521) to evaluate adjusting autoscaler burst window and increasing transient headroom for dedicated clusters supporting high-variance ecommerce traffic.

— Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 May 2028 10:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production degradation — checkout paths stalling (exec summary & next steps)

Team —

Thanks for the rapid response and the concrete mitigation. Summary for execs and the Pivotal Retail account team: 
- Impact: Pivotal Retail saw transient p99 spikes up to 35s and a short window where error rate spiked to ~5%; throughput degraded and we estimate ~3% conversion loss for affected minutes.
- Root cause (initial): cascading concurrency-cap saturation exacerbated by KV cache miss churn and autoscaler policy that doesn't open capacity for very short bursts.
- Immediate resolution: Dev/Kim raised concurrency headroom, enabled shedding, and routed to a quantized fallback — p99 dropped to ~12–15s and error rate to ~1.2% while we stabilize.

As a next step I want approval to: 
1) Apply a short-term autoscaler policy change for pr-retail-ded-02 to allow faster burst replica addition for the next 48 hours. Estimated incremental cost: $3,800 over 48 hours.
2) Offer the customer a one-time credit to offset their conversion loss and reassure account health (suggested credit: $10k).

Marcus — please escalate the cost/credit ask to sales leadership for quick approval; if we get a firm go-ahead we'll communicate to Sam and proceed.

Also: Suggest follow-up work item SUP-4521 (ops/engineering) for long-term fixes: tweak autoscaler burst window, improve prefix warm/caching heuristics, and add an emergency routing fallback in console for dedicated pools.

— Monica
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
